To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a collagen lattice modulates total protein synthesis in smooth muscles cells from SHR and WKy rats.

a three-dimensional collagen lattice modulated total protein synthesis in smooth-muscle cells (SMC), but cells from spontaneously hypertensive (SHR) rats reacted less than those from normotensive rats.

a three-dimensional cell-collagen system modulates total protein synthesis in smooth muscles from normotensive rats and spontaneously hypertensive (SHR) rats, but that cells from SHR react to this matrix less than cells from normotensives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question as to whether the metabolic properties of SMC from normotensive rats are differentially regulated by a three-dimensional type I collagen matrix in comparison with SMC from SHR.
the question of how the extracellular matrix (ECM) influences the phenotype of SMC from WKR and SHR.
the regulation of protein synthesis and cell cycle progression in SMC from SHRs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SMC from SHR have an enhanced capacity for protein synthesis in a collagen lattice culture, but this is not related to an increase in collagen synthesis.

SHR SMC are less susceptible to the influence of a three-dimensional collagen lattice compared with WKY rat SMC, and that the synthetic phenotype of SMC from both SHR and WKY rat is not influenced by a collagen lattice.
SHR SMC are less susceptible to matrix-induced changes in cell cycle distribution and protein synthesis than WKY SMC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SHR SMC are less susceptible to the influence of collagen lattice cultures compared with WKY SMC.
the three-dimensional matrix of collagen is a powerful regulator of SMC protein synthesis.
the SHR SMCs have a more active synthetic phenotype in collagen lattices than the WKY SMCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the three-dimensional matrix of collagen is an excellent tool to study the effects of hypertrophy in SMC from normotensive rats and from spontaneously hypertensive animals.
a three-dimensional collagen matrix can be a good tool to investigate the metabolic and morphologic properties of smooth muscle in hypertensive rats.
the three-dimensional collagen matrix is able to induce a more physiological phenotype in both SHR and WKY cells.
